premise.text: Explicit coverage of the old slot: Recorded attributed premise, not independently proved event: The High Court regarded termination as prima facie illegal and the plaintiff as in possession when suit was filed, granting interim relief.
premise.speaker: High Court, as reported by the Supreme Court
premise.quote:
the termination of the dealership agreement was prima facie illegal.
on the date of filing of the suit the plaintiff was in possession of the property.
the interlocutory applications, in I.A.Nos.1373 and 1497 of 2000, were allowed as prayed for.
limitations: TRUE denotes the attributed prima facie High Court conclusion.
The finding is not an authoritative final determination that termination was illegal.
The Supreme Court criticized the extent to which disputed contractual merits had been addressed at the interlocutory stage.
TRUE denotes the High Court's finding, not an independently established possession fact.
The Trial Court had reached a contrary assessment after considering the reported handover documents.
Evidence of conducting business and evidence of physical possession are not automatically interchangeable.
The Supreme Court did not finally resolve possession.
This records the procedural content of the challenged order.
The existence of the order does not establish the substantive correctness of its underlying findings.
The order operated pending disposal of the suit rather than finally deciding it.
It is not used as evidence proving the eventual Supreme Court disposition.
Composite is coverage of attributed records, not new independent legal finding.

premise.text: Explicit coverage of the old slot: Recorded attributed premise, not independently proved event: The target Court recorded the conceded change from proprietary firm to partnership and the contractual revocation clause; its view of entitlement to act was expressly prima facie.
premise.speaker: Supreme Court
premise.stage: Prima facie contractual assessment during interlocutory appeal
premise.quote:
Concededly the respondent no.1 had changed the structure of the firm from a proprietary firm to a partnership firm.
Therefore, prima facie the appellant was entitled to take action for revoking the agreement entered with the respondent no.1.
limitations: The conceded change in structure is distinguished from the separate dissolution-related account attributed to the High Court.
The source does not separately establish the precise date of the change from proprietorship to partnership.
A conceded structural change does not by itself finally determine whether prior permission existed, whether any breach persisted, or whether rectification was required.
The contract's consequences were considered for the limited interlocutory purpose.
TRUE represents the Court's expressly qualified prima facie assessment.
Entitlement to take action prima facie is not a final finding that revocation was valid.
The possible obligation to permit rectification remained unresolved.
The finding does not adjudicate possession or create a final merits determination.
Composite is coverage of attributed records, not new independent legal finding.
